column3: Violin-string core of endless nylon 6 (polyamide) filaments in the invention of W. Behringer (1968 priority); the example core of the E string has a total denier of 1435 and consists of 7 individual endless filaments of 205 denier each; covering strands of round wire 0.03 to 0.35 mm (violin to contrabass) or flat bands of aluminium alloy, chromium-nickel steel, nickel, silver or copper
column4: Statements of the patent specification and abstract: the core threads have a breaking elongation of 9 to 15 percent, a tensile strength of 80 to 110 kg/mm^2 and a modulus of elasticity of 1150 to 1350 kg/mm^2 (kilogram-force; converted here with 9.80665 N per kgf), about 30 to 50 complete twists per metre; a finished thin violin E string is about 0.54 mm in diameter and a bass string may be as large as 3.9 mm
column5: These are the ranges the specification requires of the core threads, not measurements of a named commercial string; the patent states no temperature or humidity

column3: Multifilament core of vinylidene fluoride resin (PVDF) for string instruments in the invention of Ueba, Ohashi and Sunaga (Kureha): monofilament 32 micrometre diameter, specific gravity 1.78, birefringence 38e-3; multifilament 300 d (24 filaments), S twist 0.9 per inch; the core of Example 1 is eight such yarns folded and twisted (Z, twice per inch) and heat-set for 1 h at 140 C, that of Example 2 six yarns
column4: Measurements printed in the examples: core diameter, elongation, tensile strength, creep elongation (24 h after a load of 20 percent of the tensile strength) and Young's modulus from the gradient between the points of 0.1 and 3 percent elongation at the maximum load; kg/mm^2 is kilogram-force per square millimetre (9.80665e6 Pa)
column5: Temperature and humidity of the tests are not stated; the claim requires a Young's modulus of at least 200 kg/mm^2 and the description prefers 400 to 600

column3: Violin strings compared in the patent's Table 2: commercial gut strings (trade name Eudoxa), the invention's strings (a PVDF core wound with 2 turns of a fine flat phosphor bronze wire of thickness 0.05, 0.07 and 0.10 mm for the A, D and G string on cores of 8, 8 and 6 yarns of 300 d) and commercial nylon strings (trade name Thomastik/Dominant), as unwound core and as finished string
column4: Diameter of the string and METSUKE (the table's word for weight per unit length, g/m) of the core material and of the whole string; open-string pitches A 440, D 294 and G 196 Hz
column5: The patent does not say how many strings of each kind were measured or how the core was separated; values as printed
